diagnosis: Encapsulated papillary carcinoma with invasive carcinoma of no special type (NST)
legend: Frank invasion is defined as the presence of neoplastic elements that permeate beyond the fibrous capsule with an irregular infiltrative appearance. This most commonly takes the form of invasive carcinoma NST.

legend: Encapsulated papillary carcinoma showing a thick fibrous capsule surrounding the tumour, composed of monotonous epithelial cells with mild atypia forming papillary structures.
Encapsulated papillary carcinoma showing a thick fibrous capsule and the tumour cells showing prominent papillary architecture.

Encapsulated papillary carcinoma showing an expansile, circumscribed and mostly encapsulated tumour mass comprising anastomosing papillary fronds covered by a monotonous population of columnar epithelial cells with stratified hyperchromatic nuclei. The papillary fronds project into a cystically dilated space. One area shows closely apposed tubules in the fibrous wall, which may raise concern for invasion, but as it appears confined to the fibrous area without extending into surrounding fat, is regarded as non diagnostic for invasion.
